Zimbabwe destroyed itself the day it destroyed the people who produce. Confiscating 4,500 productive commercial farms from the people who actually knew how to run them and handing them to political allies with zero farming experience is precisely how you turn Africa’s breadbasket into a country that can’t feed itself and ends up printing 100 trillion dollar notes that won’t even cover a bus fare. Mugabe did exactly that in 2000. >commercial farmland lost 3/4 of its value in a single year >food production dropped 60% over the next decade >nearly 700 companies that depended on farm exports and food processing shut down within 2 years >the economy shrank more than 6% a year and average incomes fell by more than half “Just give poor people money, bro!” And so they did with the tax base gone! >printed money to fill the hole >prices were doubling every 24 hours by late 2008 >official inflation numbers stopped being published and an independent economist calculated monthly inflation at 79.6 billion %. Communism is grand. Video Rothmus 🏴 (@Rothmus) Germany printed money until people burned banknotes for heat because firewood cost more. By late 1923, workers got paid TWICE A DAY because their wages lost value between breakfast and lunch. The spiral started when France and Belgium occupied the Ruhr after Germany missed reparations payments, German workers walked out in mass strike, and the government covered their wages by running the printing presses nonstop. $1 bought 4.2 marks in 1914 and 4.2 trillion by November 1923. People hauled pay home in wheelbarrows and suitcases while wives met husbands at the factory gate to spend the morning’s money before afternoon prices made it worthless. Gustav Stresemann introduced the Rentenmark in November, backed by mortgages on land and industry after the gold was gone, and simply cut 12 zeros off the old prices. It stabilized almost overnight. A year later the Reichsmark replaced it and the hyperinflation that erased an entire middle class’s savings was over within weeks. Fertility fell to 1.28. • England and Wales: Births fell 1.6% in 2025, while fertility dropped to an estimated 1.39. • Scotland: Births reached their lowest level since records began in 1855. Fertility hit a record-low 1.25. • Austria: Births fell to a 25-year low. Fertility hit a record-low 1.30. • Switzerland: Fertility fell again to 1.28 in 2025. • Greece: 68,467 births vs 126,916 deaths. • Malta, Spain and Lithuania recorded the EU’s lowest fertility rates: 1.01, 1.10 and 1.11. • Spain still recorded 122,167 more deaths than births in 2025, despite a small rise in births. • Finland: Fertility rose slightly to 1.30 in 2025, but remains far below 1.87 in 2010. Replacement level is roughly 2.1 children per woman. Europe’s demographic crisis is no longer limited to just a few countries. A dear friend of mine handed me this writing found from a nursing home resident and I want to share it with you... “I am 82 years old, I have 4 children, 11 grandchildren, 2 great-grandchildren and a room of 12 square meters. I no longer have a home or expensive things, but I have someone who will clean my room, prepare food and change my bedding, measure my blood pressure and weigh me. I no longer have the laughter of my grandchildren around me, I don't see them growing, hugging and arguing. Some come to me every 15 days, some every three or four months, and some never. I don't bake cakes anymore, I don't dig up the garden. I still have hobbies and I like to read, but my eyes quickly hurt. I don’t know how much longer, but I have to get used to this loneliness. Here at this home, I lead group work and help those who are worse than me as much as I can. Until recently, I read aloud to an immobile woman in the room next to me, we used to sing together, but she died the other day. They say life is getting longer. Why? When I’m alone, I can look at photos of my family and memories I brought from home. And that's all. I miss them. I hope that the next generations will understand that families are born to have a future (with children) and that they do not forget about the family even in old age.” PLEASE DON'T FORGET YOUR LOVED ONES.
